qt: to the Commission Gerald Hauser (PfE) Subject:

The Commission was forced to admit that on two occasions between 2015 and 2020, the Wuhan Institute of Virology received high amounts of gain-of-function research funding from programmes under the EU framework programme for research and innovation Horizon 20201. Gain-of-function research involves, among other things, modifying pathogens to make them more dangerous, more contagious and more deadly. The US administration2, US Congress3, the German Federal Intelligence Service4, and renowned scientists5 have now all confirmed that it is highly likely that the COVID-19 virus originated in this laboratory in Wuhan. As a result, the US administration has pulled funding for many gain-of-function projects that have the potential to trigger a pandemic6. Meanwhile, the Commission has said that it also funded a gain-of-function project in Rotterdam on the flu virus and wants to continue supporting such projects7. 1.
Which laboratories and institutes in the EU and worldwide have been receiving funding from the Commission for gain-of-function research since 2020?
Is gain-of-function research in the EU clearly regulated and policed by law?
Will the Commission follow the US administration’s lead and put a stop to or severely restrict dangerous gain-of-function research that has the potential to trigger a new pandemic?
at: (English version) to the Commission Gerald Hauser (PfE) (21 October 2025) Subject: Highly dangerous EU-supported gain-of-function research The Commission was forced to admit that on two occasions between 2015 and 2020, the Wuhan Institute of Virology received high amounts of gain-of-function research funding from programmes under the EU framework programme for research and innovation Horizon 2020 (1). Gain-of-function research involves, among other things, modifying pathogens to make them more dangerous, more contagious and more deadly. The US administration (2), US Congress (3), the German Federal Intelligence Service (4), and renowned scientists (5) have now all confirmed that it is highly likely that the COVID-19 virus originated in this laboratory in Wuhan. As a result, the US administration has pulled funding for many gain-of-function projects that have the potential to trigger a pandemic (6). Meanwhile, the Commission has said that it also funded a gain-of-function project in Rotterdam on the flu virus and wants to continue supporting such projects (7). 1.Which laboratories and institutes in the EU and worldwide have been receiving funding from the Commission for gain-of-function research since 2020? 2.Is gain-of-function research in the EU clearly regulated and policed by law? 3.Will the Commission follow the US administration’s lead and put a stop to or severely restrict dangerous gain-of-function research that has the potential to trigger a new pandemic? (10 December 2025) We refer the honourable member to the answer to Parliamentary Question E-002369/2025, detailing the Commission's risk management measures, eligibility criteria, and security checks to support gainof-function research on influenza.
